title: Der Nebensatz: weil, dass, wenn
summary: The A2→B1 gate: weil, dass, and wenn send the verb to the very end of the clause

blocks.title: Der Verb-Umzug: weil, dass, wenn
blocks.body: In a **main clause**, the verb sits in position two. But after **weil** (because), **dass** (that) and **wenn** (if/when), the verb packs its bags and moves to the **very end** of that clause: *Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Berlin wohne* (not: weil ich wohne in Berlin). This is the single biggest word-order shift in German — worth slowing down for.
blocks.callout: Trick: think of the subclause verb as waiting by the door until everyone else has walked in.

pairs.left: Ich bin müde. — main clause, verb 2nd
pairs.right: …, weil ich müde bin. — subclause, verb LAST
pairs.note: Same idea, but weil sends bin all the way to the end.

pairs.right: Ich glaube, dass das stimmt. — dass-clause, verb last
pairs.note: stimmt moves to the end after dass.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence correctly puts the verb at the end after weil?
options: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich bin krank.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil bin ich krank.
blocks.explain: weil ich krank bin — subject first, then everything else, verb (bin) dead last.

blocks.prompt: Complete: 'Ich gehe nicht raus, ___.' (because it's raining — use weil and es regnet)
blocks.explain: weil es regnet — es is the subject, regnet the verb, and it has to wait until the end.

blocks.title: dass nach Meinungsverben
blocks.body: **dass** often follows opinion and reporting verbs: *ich glaube, dass…*, *ich finde, dass…*, *ich weiß, dass…*. Same rule applies — verb to the end of the *dass*-clause: *Ich glaube, dass Berlin teuer wird* (I think that Berlin is getting expensive).

blocks.title: Baue einen weil-Satz
blocks.prompt: Build a sentence explaining why, using weil.
blocks.sample: Ich bin müde, weil ich spät ins Bett gegangen bin.

blocks.scene: Lena explains over coffee why she loves living in Berlin.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Ich liebe Berlin, weil hier immer etwas los ist.
lines.en: I love Berlin because there's always something going on here.
lines.spotlight: weil … los ist — the verb (ist) sits at the very end.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Und was, wenn es mal zu viel wird?
lines.en: And what if it gets too much sometimes?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Wenn ich Ruhe brauche, fahre ich einfach in den Park.
lines.en: When I need quiet, I just go to the park.
lines.spotlight: Wenn-clause first: brauche sits at the end of the wenn-part, then fahre follows right after the comma.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ich glaube, dass das eine gute Idee ist.
lines.en: I think that's a good idea.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Genau! Und ich finde, dass Berlin trotzdem meine Stadt bleibt.
lines.en: Exactly! And I think Berlin stays my city anyway.

questions.q: What does Lena do when she needs quiet?

blocks.prompt: Finish three sentences: one with weil, one with dass, one with wenn. Talk about your own life in Berlin or your city.
